children: Copper prices are higher in early Asian trading hours, supported by tight mine supply and low inventories, CICC Wealth Futures Research Institute analysts write in a note. However, elevated prices continue to weigh on downstream demand, while spot market transactions remain subdued despite sellers lowering offers, they say. Prices are likely to remain range-bound at high levels in the near term, with supply tightness and low inventories providing a floor, they add. Investors will watch for a recovery in downstream orders as production resumes. The three-month LME copper contract is up 0.4% at $14,595.50 a ton.(jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
